# attribution 01-vectors

Per-(user, day) miner attribution (scoring-port-contract §3): C3 day-close membership (last member_joined with epoch ≤ d; a mid-day switch gives the WHOLE day to the day-close group), C2 start-of-day binding (core timestamps: bound_at ≤ d@00:00Z < unbound_at — a mid-day bind attributes from d+1, a mid-day unbind still attributes d, an exact-midnight bind attributes that day), the per-day clamp min(20, max(0, daily_score)), miner sums, active_members (strict > 50) and eligibility (≥ 3). Recompute from the inputs; your outputs MUST equal `expected` exactly.

## Dual-role leader (r4)

`binding_events` carries a `role` field (`miner` | `validator`) — map `miner_hotkey_bind`/`miner_hotkey_unbind` to `role: "miner"` and `validator_hotkey_bind`/`validator_hotkey_unbind` to `role: "validator"`. **Attribution reads MINER bindings only.** Leader `usr_evt_leader_N` (group `grp-3`) holds three bindings: a validator hotkey bound BEFORE its miner hotkey (2026-05-01), the miner hotkey (2026-06-01), and a second validator hotkey bound mid-window (2026-07-02). Every one of `usr_evt_u5|u6|u7`'s days MUST attribute to the miner hotkey (`test-keys/sr25519-miner-dual.json`) — "first binding seen", "earliest bound_at" and "latest bound_at" each pick a validator hotkey on at least one day, so this case fails for any role-blind implementation. Where two MINER bindings are somehow active at the same instant (the platform keeps at most one), the latest `bound_at` wins, ties broken by ascending `hotkey_ss58` — a determinism guard so input order cannot change the result.
